title: Insurance Claim (Third-Party Billing): Non-Covered Write-Off of Take-Home Convenience Items
content:
**Denials desk note.** On a Commercial PPO, Commercial HMO or Marketplace claim in denied status for an Outpatient Surgery Account, this rule takes the take-home convenience items off the claim as one write-off entry with the write-off reason NONCOVERED_NO_WAIVER, carrying the claim's current denial reason code; any other claim gets nothing here.

The take-home convenience items are billed on the Outpatient Surgery Account of the patient's Hospital Account (Encounter Billing); the claim is the Insurance Claim (Third-Party Billing) for that account.

**What the write-off amount replaces.** For the take-home convenience items of a claim closed under this rule, and only for them, the amount written off as non-covered with no waiver is the convenience value rather than their charges; small items on Riverbend's outpatient-surgery small-item list, the services closed on the member's decision, small items on Riverbend's observation and emergency small-item list, self-administered drugs and the services closed on the patient's external-review decision are written off under their own rules, and every other denied amount is written off in full by the hospital, never billed to the patient, when its route ends in a write-off: timely filing expired (no timely-filing proof), no authorization obtained (no authorization, notification, emergency exemption or retro authorization), non-covered with no waiver (no advance waiver on file), appeals exhausted (the last available level upheld the denial), or below the appeal threshold (a denied amount at or below the payer class's small-denial write-off amount that is not worth appealing).

**What stays on the claim.** The convenience-item charges above the convenience value stay on the claim as the contractual remainder, which Riverbend's month-end contractual close posts on the last calendar day of the month.

## Booking the write-off: `write_off_noncovered_convenience_item_58e216c4`
**Capability.** Writes off, on one denied insurance claim, the value of take-home convenience items that no payer covers and for which no advance financial-responsibility waiver is on file: one write-off entry with the write-off reason NONCOVERED_NO_WAIVER and the claim's current denial reason code, dated today, lowering the amount still expected from the payer on that claim by the same figure. The patient is never billed for it; the claim's status does not change.

**Invocation.** An agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `write_off_noncovered_convenience_item_58e216c4` and then calls it.

**Parameters**
| Parameter | Meaning and format |
|---|---|
| `claim_id` | the reference number of the insurance claim whose convenience items are written off, as shown by the claim lookup for the patient |
| `amount_usd` | the convenience-item value being written off, in USD, 2 decimal places, positive magnitude, already rounded to the cent by the caller; posted exactly as given |

**Return.** A text receipt: "Write-off <entry_id> posted on claim <claim_id>: <amount_usd> USD, reason NONCOVERED_NO_WAIVER, denial code <carc_code>; amount still expected from the payer <payer_balance> USD." The entry reference identifies the new claim activity entry, the denial code is the claim's denial reason code copied onto it, and the payer balance is the new amount still expected from the payer (USD, 2 decimal places). The receipt appearing is the success signal.
